teile.einleitung: The Dead Sea Scrolls are very old manuscripts that were found in caves near Qumran from 1947 onwards. They are among the most important finds in archaeology and contain the oldest known Bible texts.
wichtigste: The first scrolls were discovered in 1947.
Scrolls or fragments were found in 11 caves.
Most of it is written in Hebrew.
The Great Isaiah Scroll contains the Book of Isaiah almost complete.
The biblical texts are about 1,000 years older than the oldest complete manuscripts known until then.
Not a single fragment of the Book of Esther was found.

abschnitte.text: In **1947**, Bedouins discovered old clay jars with scrolls in a cave near **Qumran** by the Dead Sea. In the following years researchers kept searching. In all, scrolls or fragments were found in **11 caves**. Many texts survive only in small pieces, which had to be laboriously put together.

About a quarter of the texts are **biblical texts**. The best known is the **Great Isaiah Scroll** from Cave 1. It contains the Book of **Isaiah** almost complete. The Qumran texts are **about 1,000 years older** than the oldest complete Hebrew Bible manuscripts from the Middle Ages known until then. They show how carefully the text was copied over a long time. Only of the Book of **Esther** was not a single fragment found.

Most of it is written in **Hebrew**, other texts in Aramaic or Greek. Besides biblical texts there are rules of a community, prayers and commentaries. Special is the **Copper Scroll**: it is scratched into metal and **lists hiding places of treasures**. Whether these treasures ever existed is not known.

The community of Qumran is most often linked with the **Essenes**. They were a Jewish group who lived very strictly by religious rules. This interpretation is not undisputed among researchers, however. Today important scrolls are on display in the **Shrine of the Book** at the Israel Museum in Jerusalem. The roof of the building has the shape of a jar lid.

gewusst: The texts date from roughly the 3rd century BC to the 1st century AD.
In all, remains of about 900 different manuscripts from Qumran are known.

teile.einleitung: “Sola gratia” means “by grace alone”. According to this principle of the Reformation, people cannot earn salvation. They receive it as a free, undeserved gift from God.
wichtigste: “Sola gratia” means “by grace alone”.
According to this principle, salvation is an undeserved gift from God.
The Reformers appealed especially to Augustine.
In 1517 Luther criticised the sale of indulgences.
In 1525 Luther answered Erasmus with “De servo arbitrio”.
The Reformers rejected Pelagianism.

abschnitte.text: In theology, **grace** means God's free turning towards human beings. The principle **“sola gratia”** says: people cannot earn salvation through achievement. They are given it without deserving it. Together with “sola fide” and “sola scriptura”, this principle is one of the core ideas of the Reformation. Luther also spoke of **alien righteousness**, “iustitia aliena”, which comes from Christ and is granted to the person.

People were already arguing about this question in the 5th century. The monk **Pelagius** stressed that people could live good lives by their own will. The Church Father **Augustine** of Hippo countered that people depend entirely on God's grace. The teaching of Pelagius is called **Pelagianism** and was rejected by the Church. The Reformers appealed especially to Augustine. Luther was also a monk in the order of the Augustinian Hermits.

In Luther's time the Church sold **indulgences**. They were meant to shorten the punishments for sins. Preachers such as Johann Tetzel promoted them. In 1517 Luther criticised this practice in his **95 Theses**. In his view it made God's grace seem something that could be bought, but forgiveness could not be acquired with money.

The scholar **Erasmus of Rotterdam** published a work on free will in 1524, “De libero arbitrio”. He thought that people could cooperate in their salvation. In 1525 Luther answered with **“De servo arbitrio”**, “On the Bondage of the Will”. In it he wrote that in matters of salvation the will is not free but depends entirely on God's grace. The dispute showed how differently humanists and Reformers saw the human being.

gewusst: Erasmus lived and worked in Basel for many years and is buried in Basel Minster.
The well-known song “Amazing Grace” is also about God's undeserved grace.

teile.einleitung: The Septuagint is the oldest Greek translation of the Hebrew Bible. It came into being from the 3rd century BC for Jews who spoke Greek. Later it became the Old Testament of the first Christians.
wichtigste: The Septuagint is a Greek translation of the Hebrew Bible.
According to tradition it came into being in Alexandria in Egypt.
First the Torah, that is, the five Books of Moses, was translated.
The name means “seventy”; the abbreviation is LXX.
According to the Letter of Aristeas, 72 translators worked on it.
The early Christians adopted it as their Old Testament.

abschnitte.text: After the conquests of Alexander the Great, **Greek** became the most important language in the eastern Mediterranean. Many Jews lived outside Israel and no longer understood Hebrew well. So their holy writings were translated into Greek. First, in the 3rd century BC, the translation of the **Torah**, the five Books of Moses, was made. The other books followed over the course of about two centuries.

In **Alexandria** in Egypt lived a large Jewish community that spoke Greek. An old text, the **Letter of Aristeas**, tells a legend: King Ptolemy II Philadelphus wanted the translation for his famous library. Six scholars came from each of the twelve tribes of Israel, 72 in all. They finished the work in 72 days. Historians regard this story as largely legendary.

“Septuaginta” is the Latin word for **seventy**. The number recalls the roughly seventy translators of the legend. The abbreviation is written **LXX**, which is seventy in Roman numerals. Scholars still use this abbreviation today. The Septuagint also contains some books that are missing from the Hebrew Bible.

abschnitte.titel: The Bible of the first Christians
abschnitte.text: The early Christians often spoke Greek and therefore read the Septuagint. The **New Testament** often quotes the Old Testament in its version. A well-known example is Isaiah 7:14: in Hebrew it says “alma”, young woman, but in the Septuagint “parthenos”. The Gospel of Matthew quotes this Greek version in the Christmas story. In the Orthodox Church the Septuagint is still regarded as the authoritative form of the Old Testament.

Important texts of the Septuagint survive in great **manuscripts** from the 4th and 5th centuries. One of the most famous is the **Codex Sinaiticus**. The scholar Konstantin von Tischendorf discovered it in the 19th century in St Catherine's Monastery on Sinai. In 1844 he found the first leaves, and in 1859 he received the main part. The codex also contains the complete New Testament.

gewusst: The Codex Sinaiticus is now spread over several places; the largest part is in London.
Many words of the Septuagint such as “Genesis” or “Exodus” are still the names of biblical books today.

teile.einleitung: Samuel is an important figure in the Old Testament. Even as a child he heard the voice of God. Later he became a prophet and anointed the first kings of Israel.
wichtigste: Samuel's mother was called Hannah.
Hannah had asked God for a child for a long time.
Samuel grew up with the priest Eli in the sanctuary.
In the night he heard a voice calling his name.
He answered: “Speak, for your servant is listening.”
As a prophet, Samuel anointed Saul as the first king of Israel.

abschnitte.text: Samuel's mother was called **Hannah**. For a long time she had no child and was very sad about it. In the sanctuary at Shiloh she prayed to God and asked **for a child**. She promised that the child would serve God. When Samuel was born, her joy was great. She thanked God with a song.

When Samuel was still small, Hannah brought him to the sanctuary, to the priest **Eli**. Samuel grew up there and helped with the service. Every year his mother brought him a new robe. Samuel learned how to serve God.

One night Samuel heard **a voice calling his name**. He ran to Eli, but Eli had not called. This happened **three times**. Then Eli realised that God was calling the boy. He told Samuel to answer: **“Speak, for your servant is listening.”** That is how God spoke to Samuel for the first time.

When Samuel was grown up, he became a **prophet**. A prophet announces what God wants to say to people. Samuel also led the people of Israel as a judge. When the people wanted a king, Samuel anointed **Saul** as the first king. Later he anointed the young **David**, who became king after Saul.

gewusst: Two books of the Bible bear Samuel's name: the first and the second Book of Samuel.
The name Samuel is often explained as “God has heard”.

teile.einleitung: The Star of Bethlehem is part of the Christmas story. According to the Gospel of Matthew, it led wise men from the East to the newborn Jesus. To this day the star on the Christmas tree recalls this story.
wichtigste: Only the Gospel of Matthew tells of the star.
The wise men first looked for the new king in Jerusalem.
The star stopped over the place where the child was.
When they saw the star again, they were overjoyed.
Painters often show it like a comet with a tail.
Some researchers suspect Jupiter and Saturn close together behind it.

abschnitte.text: Only the **Gospel of Matthew** tells of the star. Wise men from the East saw a star rise and took it as a sign of a new king. They set out on a long journey. First they looked for the child in the capital, **Jerusalem**, at the court of King Herod. There they learned that the expected king was to be born in **Bethlehem**.

When the wise men travelled on, they saw the star again. The Bible says that they had **very great joy**. The star went ahead of them and **stopped** over the place where the child was. So they found Jesus and his mother Mary. They knelt down and brought their gifts.

Many painters show the star like a **comet** with a long, shining tail. A famous example is a fresco by the painter **Giotto** in Padua from the early 14th century. That is why the star is often shown with a tail on nativity scenes too. The Bible says only that it was a star.

Researchers have long wondered what might lie behind the star. Some think of the planets **Jupiter and Saturn**, which stood close together in the sky a few years before the start of our calendar. The astronomer **Johannes Kepler** already put forward this idea. Others think of a comet or a new bright star. Nobody knows for certain, and many see in the star above all a picture of God's guidance.

At Christmas we meet the star everywhere. Many people put a **star on top of the Christmas tree**, some a glass tip instead. Stars hang in windows and decorate streets. Around Epiphany, the **star singers** carry a star from house to house. It recalls that the star showed the way to the child.

gewusst: A European space probe that visited Halley's Comet in 1986 was named after the painter Giotto.
In the Church of the Nativity in Bethlehem, a silver star marks the place where Jesus is said to have been born.

teile.einleitung: A blessing is a good wish that points to God. Whoever blesses wishes a person good things from God and entrusts them to his protection. There are blessings in church services, at parting, before a meal or before a journey.
wichtigste: To bless means to wish a person good things from God.
In a church service the blessing comes at the end.
A very old blessing begins with “The Lord bless you and keep you”.
During a blessing the hands are often raised or spread out.
At Christmas and Easter the Pope gives the blessing “Urbi et orbi”.
Greetings such as “God keep you” also contain a small blessing.

abschnitte.text: The German word for **bless**, “segnen”, comes from the Latin “signare”, which means “to mark with a sign”. This usually means the sign of the cross. Whoever blesses asks God to protect a person and give them good things. So a blessing is a wish that does not come from a person alone but trusts in God. Pastors can bless, but so can parents, grandparents or friends.

In many churches the **service** ends with the blessing. The pastor lifts the hands or spreads them out over the congregation. The gesture shows that the blessing comes from God and is meant for everyone. Then people go home with this good wish and into the new week. In the Reformed churches of Switzerland this is just as usual as in Catholic ones.

One of the oldest blessings is in the Old Testament, in the 4th Book of Moses. It is called the **Aaronic blessing** because it was entrusted to Aaron and his sons, the priests. It begins with the words “The Lord bless you and keep you”. It goes on to say that God makes his face shine upon you and gives you peace. This blessing is still spoken today in Jewish and Christian services.

At Christmas and Easter the Pope gives a special blessing. It is called **“Urbi et orbi”**, which means “to the city and to the world”. This means the city of Rome and the whole world. The Pope speaks it from the balcony of St Peter's Basilica. Many people all over the world follow it on television or on the internet.

There are blessings in everyday life too. At parting, in some regions people say **“Behüt dich Gott”**, which means: may God protect you. Before a meal people wish each other “Gesegnete Mahlzeit”, a blessed meal. Before a journey one can speak a **travel blessing** and ask God to protect the travellers. Even the greeting “Grüss Gott” originally contains a good wish.

gewusst: The words “Grüss Gott” originally mean “God greet you”, so they are a small blessing.
The Aaronic blessing is over 2,000 years old and is still spoken in almost exactly the same words today.

teile.einleitung: The Sistine Chapel is a famous chapel in the Vatican in Rome. Michelangelo painted its ceiling and the altar wall with huge pictures from the Bible. Here the cardinals also elect a new pope.
wichtigste: The Sistine Chapel stands in the Apostolic Palace in the Vatican.
It is named after Pope Sixtus IV, who had it built from 1475.
Michelangelo painted the ceiling from 1508 to 1512.
The best-known picture is “The Creation of Adam”.
On the altar wall Michelangelo painted “The Last Judgement”.
The conclave to elect the pope takes place in the chapel.

abschnitte.text: The Sistine Chapel is part of the **Apostolic Palace** in the Vatican. Pope **Sixtus IV** had it built from 1475, which is why it bears his name. The room is about 40 metres long and 13 metres wide. Soon famous artists such as Botticelli and Perugino painted the side walls. Today the chapel is part of the **Vatican Museums** and is visited by millions of people every year.

From 1508 to 1512, **Michelangelo** Buonarroti painted the enormous ceiling. He actually saw himself mainly as a sculptor. He often worked on a high scaffold with his head tilted back. The nine main pictures in the middle show stories from **Genesis**, the first Book of Moses. They include the creation of the world and the story of Noah.

The most famous picture on the ceiling is **“The Creation of Adam”**. God stretches out his finger to give life to the first human being. The fingertips of God and Adam almost touch. These two hands are among the best-known motifs in the history of art. Today they can be seen on posters, mugs and in many films.

Michelangelo painted in the technique of **fresco**. The paint is applied to lime plaster that is still damp. As it dries, it bonds firmly with the wall and lasts for centuries. Because the plaster dries quickly, a piece had to be finished every day. Later, from 1536 to 1541, Michelangelo painted the huge fresco **“The Last Judgement”** on the altar wall, with Christ as the judge.

When a new pope is elected, the cardinals gather in the Sistine Chapel. This assembly is called the **conclave**, from the Latin “cum clave”, with a key. The cardinals are shut off from the outside world. After each round of voting the ballot papers are burned. **White smoke** from the chimney shows that a new pope has been elected; black smoke means: no agreement yet.

gewusst: From 1980 to 1994 the frescoes were cleaned, and afterwards the colours shone much brighter than before.
The Swiss Guard protects the pope and so also the Apostolic Palace.

teile.einleitung: “Sola fide” is Latin and means “by faith alone”. The principle comes from the Reformation: a person is made right with God because they believe, not because of their good works. It is one of the most important ideas of Martin Luther.
wichtigste: “Sola fide” means “by faith alone”.
It is about justification: God declares the sinner righteous.
For Luther the Bible passage Romans 1:17 was central.
In Romans 3:28 Luther added the word “alone”.
He called the Letter of James an “epistle of straw”.
According to Luther, the believer is “simul iustus et peccator”.

abschnitte.text: **Justification** is a theological technical term. It means that God **declares** sinful people **righteous**, that is, accepts them and forgives them. The question was: how does this happen? According to Reformation teaching, by **faith** in Jesus Christ alone and not through one's own achievements. “Sola fide” belongs together with “sola gratia” and “sola scriptura” among the well-known principles of the Reformation.

For a long time Luther suffered from the fear of not being good enough before God. While working on the Bible he came across **Romans 1:17**: “The righteous shall live by faith.” There Paul quotes the prophet Habakkuk. Luther now understood that God's righteousness makes a person righteous through faith. He later called this liberating insight his **tower experience**, after a tower room in the monastery at Wittenberg. When exactly it happened is disputed among researchers.

In his translation of the Bible, Luther wrote in **Romans 3:28** that a person is made righteous “without the works of the law, by faith alone”. The word **“alone”** is not in the Greek text. His opponents therefore accused him of falsifying it. Luther defended his choice in 1530 in the “Open Letter on Translating”. He said that this is how one speaks in German and that the sense was rightly captured.

The **Letter of James** says that faith without works is dead. Luther found little of the gospel of justification in it and scornfully called it an **“epistle of straw”**. For Luther, good works were not unimportant, but they are the result of faith, not its precondition. The Catholic Church, on the other hand, stressed that faith and works belong together. In 1999 Lutherans and Catholics signed a joint declaration in which they moved closer together on basic questions of justification.

abschnitte.titel: Righteous and a sinner at the same time
abschnitte.text: Luther described the believing person with the formula **“simul iustus et peccator”**. That means “at the same time righteous and a sinner”. Before God the believer is declared righteous. In himself, however, he remains a person who makes mistakes. According to Luther, this tension is part of Christian life.

gewusst: The joint declaration on the doctrine of justification was signed in Augsburg in 1999.
In some editions of Luther's Bible, the sentence from Romans 1:17 is especially highlighted.

teile.einleitung: “Sola scriptura” means “by Scripture alone”. For the Reformers, the Bible was the highest standard for faith and teaching. In Zurich, Huldrych Zwingli put this principle into practice with particular determination.
wichtigste: “Sola scriptura” means “by Scripture alone”.
The Bible is regarded as the “norma normans”, the highest guideline.
In 1521 at Worms, Luther refused to recant unless he was refuted from Scripture.
In 1546 the Council of Trent placed tradition on the same level as the Bible.
From 1519 Zwingli preached continuously on the Gospel of Matthew at the Grossmünster.
In 1516 Erasmus published the Greek New Testament in Basel.

abschnitte.text: The Reformers wanted to base faith on the **Bible** again. According to the principle **“sola scriptura”**, Holy Scripture is the only binding guideline for faith and teaching. It is called the **“norma normans”**, the standard that sets the norm and by which everything is measured. Confessions of faith, by contrast, count as “norma normata”, a derived norm. They carry weight only if they agree with the Bible.

In 1521 Luther had to appear before Emperor Charles V and the estates of the Empire at the **Diet of Worms**. He was asked to recant his writings. Luther declared that he would recant only if he were refuted by the testimony of Scripture or by clear reasoning. His **conscience** was captive to the word of God. Afterwards he was placed under the imperial ban.

On 1 January 1519, **Huldrych Zwingli** began his work at the **Grossmünster** in Zurich. He broke with the prescribed order of readings and expounded the **Gospel of Matthew** chapter by chapter. This continuous exposition is called “lectio continua”. In 1525 he set up the **Prophezei**, a theological school. There biblical texts were translated and explained together from Hebrew and Greek. The Zurich Bible also came out of it.

To read the Bible accurately, one needed the **original languages**. In 1516 **Erasmus of Rotterdam** published the New Testament in Greek with the Basel printer Johann Froben, together with a Latin translation. Luther and Zwingli worked with this edition. Printing helped Bibles to spread in large numbers. Many people could now read the Bible in their own language.

The Catholic Church saw this differently. The **Council of Trent** declared in 1546 that Holy Scripture and the unwritten traditions were to be received with equal reverence. So **church tradition** stands on the same level as the Bible. In this way the Catholic Church deliberately set itself apart from the Reformation principle of Scripture. To this day this is an important difference between the denominations.

gewusst: The Zurich Bible appeared in 1531 as a complete Bible with Christoph Froschauer, a few years before Luther's complete Bible of 1534.
The Grossmünster with its two towers is still a landmark of Zurich today.

teile.einleitung: A scriptorium was the writing room of a medieval monastery. Here monks carefully copied books by hand and decorated them with pictures. Without this work many old texts would have been lost.
wichtigste: In the scriptorium, monks copied books by hand.
The word comes from the Latin “scribere”, to write.
People wrote on parchment made from animal skin, usually with a goose feather.
Elaborately decorated first letters are called initials.
Carolingian minuscule is the basis of our lower-case letters.
The Codex Abrogans in St Gallen is regarded as the oldest book in the German language.

abschnitte.text: Before printing was invented, every book had to be written **by hand**. In many monasteries there was a room of its own for this, the **scriptorium**. The name comes from the Latin “scribere”, to write. The monks worked in silence and needed plenty of light, so they usually wrote by day. A thick book often took months or even years.

Paper was unknown in Europe for a long time. People wrote on **parchment**, which was made from the skins of calves, sheep or goats. The skin was cleaned, stretched and scraped thin. Writing was done with a **bird's feather**, usually a goose quill, which was cut at an angle and dipped in ink. Because parchment was expensive, old texts were sometimes scraped off and new ones written over them. Such a sheet is called a **palimpsest**.

Many manuscripts were splendidly decorated. At the start of a chapter there is often an **initial**, a large, elaborately decorated first letter. It is painted in colour and decorated with gold, tendrils or small figures. The art of decorating manuscripts with pictures is called **book illumination**. Some pages are real works of art.

In the time of **Charlemagne**, around the year 800, a new script came into being: **Carolingian minuscule**. It was clear and easy to read and spread throughout the Frankish Empire. Our **lower-case letters** of today developed from it. So whoever writes an a or a g today is using forms that are over 1,000 years old.

A famous scriptorium was in the **Abbey of St Gallen**. The **Abbey Library** of St Gallen still keeps many valuable manuscripts today. They include the **Codex Abrogans**, a Latin and Old High German dictionary from the 8th century. It is regarded as the oldest surviving book in the German language. The Abbey Precinct of St Gallen is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

gewusst: Monks sometimes wrote little complaints in the margin, for example that their hand hurt or that it was cold.
For one large book, the skins of many animals were needed.

teile.einleitung: Scholasticism was the learning of the scholars of the Middle Ages. It tried to understand and justify the Christian faith with reason, often with the help of the philosopher Aristotle.
wichtigste: Scholasticism was practised in monastery schools and universities.
In “Sic et non”, Abelard set contradictory statements side by side.
The Sentences of Peter Lombard were for a long time the most important textbook.
Philosophy was regarded as the “handmaid of theology”.
Among the scholastics, Averroes was simply called “the Commentator”.
Well-known Franciscans were Bonaventure, Duns Scotus and William of Ockham.

abschnitte.text: The word comes from the Latin “schola”, school. The scholars of Scholasticism taught at monastery schools and later at the first **universities**, for example in Paris and Oxford. They asked questions, collected reasons for and against, and looked for an answer. **Philosophy** was regarded as the **“handmaid of theology”**: it was meant to help people understand the faith.

In his work **“Sic et non”**, “Yes and No”, **Peter Abelard** set contradictory statements of the Church Fathers side by side. Students were to learn to resolve such contradictions. The **Sentences of Peter Lombard** were the basis of theological study for centuries. Many scholars wrote their own explanations of them.

In the 12th and 13th centuries, the works of the Greek philosopher **Aristotle** became newly known in the West. Much of it came through Arab scholars. The Andalusian philosopher **Averroes** wrote such important explanations of Aristotle that the scholastics simply called him **“the Commentator”**. The best-known scholastic is **Thomas Aquinas**.

For a long time the scholars argued about **universals**, that is, general terms such as “human being” or “tree”. Do they really exist, or are they only names? **Nominalism** holds that general terms are **mere names**. An important representative was the English Franciscan **William of Ockham**. **“Ockham's razor”** is named after him: explanations should not be made more complicated than necessary.

Many scholastics were given Latin honorary titles. The Franciscan **Bonaventure** was called **“Doctor seraphicus”**. **John Duns Scotus** was called **“Doctor subtilis”** because of his sharp thinking. He is linked with the term **“haecceity”**, the “thisness” that makes something exactly this one thing. Thomas Aquinas was called “Doctor angelicus”.

gewusst: In the 13th century the University of Paris was the most important centre of Scholasticism.
Ockham himself never used the expression “razor”; it only came into use later.

teile.einleitung: The Swiss Bishops' Conference is the association of the Catholic bishops of Switzerland. It was founded as early as 1863 and is regarded as the first bishops' conference in the world.
wichtigste: The Swiss Bishops' Conference was founded in 1863.
It is regarded as the first bishops' conference in the world.
Its members are the bishops, the auxiliary bishops and the abbots of Einsiedeln and Saint-Maurice.
A term as president lasts three years.
Felix Gmür was president from 2019 to 2024; since January 2025 it has been Charles Morerod.
The general secretariat is in Fribourg.

abschnitte.text: The **Swiss Bishops' Conference** was founded in **1863**. It is regarded as the **first bishops' conference in the world**. Later, similar conferences came into being in many countries. There the bishops discuss together questions that affect the whole Catholic Church in Switzerland. The first president came from the diocese of **Sion**.

The conference includes the bishops of the six Swiss **dioceses** and the **auxiliary bishops**, who support a bishop. In addition there are the **abbots of Einsiedeln and Saint-Maurice**. These two old monasteries each lead a small church territory of their own, a **territorial abbey**. That is why their abbots are members like a bishop.

The conference elects a **president**. A term lasts **three years**. From 2019 to 2024 **Felix Gmür**, the Bishop of Basel, was president. Since **January 2025** the president has been **Charles Morerod**, Bishop of Lausanne, Geneva and Fribourg (as of 2025). The **general secretariat** is in **Fribourg**.

The Bishops' Conference speaks out on questions of faith, but also on social issues. Because in Switzerland the cantonal churches manage a lot of money, it works closely with the **Roman Catholic Central Conference**. Together they support tasks for the whole of Switzerland.

gewusst: The Abbey of Saint-Maurice in Valais has existed since the year 515 and is regarded as one of the oldest monasteries in the West with no break in its history.
Einsiedeln Abbey is an important place of pilgrimage with the famous Black Madonna.

teile.einleitung: The creation story stands right at the beginning of the Bible, in the first Book of Moses. It tells how God creates the world in six days and rests on the seventh day.
wichtigste: On the first day God created light.
On the second day he made the sky.
On the third day the first plants grew.
On the fourth day came the sun, moon and stars, on the fifth fish and birds.
On the sixth day God created human beings in his own image.
On the seventh day God rested and found everything very good.

abschnitte.text: The Bible begins with the words: “In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.” At first everything was dark and empty. On the **first day** God said: “Let there be light.” So he separated the **light** from the darkness, day from night. On the **second day** he made the **sky**, which separates the waters above from the waters below.

On the **third day** the water gathered together and dry land appeared. Then the first **plants** grew: grass, herbs and trees with fruit. On the **fourth day** God set the **sun, moon and stars** in the sky. They were to give light and to mark days, months and years.

On the **fifth day** God filled the water with **fish** and the sky with **birds**. On the **sixth day** he created the land animals. Then God created **human beings in his own image**. This means that people are like God in a special way and are meant to look after the earth. In the end God looked at everything and found it **very good**.

On the **seventh day** God rested from his work. That is why the Sabbath is a **day of rest** for Jews and Sunday for Christians. Many people do not understand the story as a scientific report. They see in it a story that says: the world is wanted, ordered and good.

gewusst: Right at the start, the Bible contains two different creation stories; the second tells of Adam and Eve in the Garden of Eden.
Our week of seven days is closely connected with this story.

teile.einleitung: Hospital chaplains accompany sick people, their relatives and the staff in the hospital. They listen, help with worries and questions about meaning, and pray when that is wanted. In Switzerland they often work on behalf of the regional churches.
wichtigste: Hospital chaplaincy accompanies patients and relatives in difficult times.
In many Swiss hospitals, Reformed and Catholic chaplains work together ecumenically.
Chaplaincy is open to everyone, including people with no religious affiliation.
Conversations are protected by professional secrecy under Art. 321 of the Criminal Code.
“Spiritual care” means attending to the spiritual needs of sick people.
In 2015 the first professorship for spiritual care in Switzerland was created at the University of Zurich.

abschnitte.text: Anyone who lies sick in hospital often has many questions and worries. **Hospital chaplains** visit people at the bedside, listen and take time. They talk about fears, hopes and questions of meaning. If asked, they pray, bless or hold a service. **Relatives** and hospital staff can also turn to them.

In many Swiss hospitals, chaplaincy is organised **ecumenically**. Reformed and Catholic chaplains work in a joint team. They visit people of every background and every religion, including those with no denomination. Nobody is converted; it is about accompanying people. In some hospitals there are also chaplains from other religious communities.

What you confide in a chaplain stays secret. Professional secrecy under **Art. 321 of the Criminal Code** counts clergy among the professions bound to confidentiality, like doctors and lawyers. Anyone who betrays a confided secret can be punished. That is why patients can speak openly. This trust is very important for chaplaincy.

Today people in healthcare often speak of **spiritual care**. It means attending to the spiritual needs of sick people, that is, meaning, hope and faith. Chaplains work with doctors and nurses in doing so. On 1 October 2015, the first professorship for spiritual care in Switzerland was created at the Faculty of Theology of the **University of Zurich**. It was funded by the Catholic and Reformed churches in the canton of Zurich. The first professor was the theologian **Simon Peng-Keller**, who also teaches medical students.

gewusst: Many hospitals have a quiet room in which people of any religion can find peace.
The Zurich professorship for spiritual care was at first limited to six years.

teile.einleitung: The Sonderbund War of 1847 was the last war on Swiss soil. Seven Catholic-conservative cantons faced the liberal cantons of the Federal Diet. After the short war, the modern federal state was founded in 1848.
wichtigste: The Sonderbund was an alliance of Catholic-conservative cantons.
It included Lucerne, Uri, Schwyz, Obwalden and Nidwalden, Zug, Fribourg and Valais.
The closure of the Aargau monasteries in 1841 and the call of the Jesuits to Lucerne in 1844 sharpened the dispute.
General Guillaume-Henri Dufour led the troops of the Federal Diet.
In November 1847 the war lasted barely four weeks.
Afterwards, the Swiss federal state was created in 1848.

abschnitte.text: In the first half of the 19th century, Switzerland was a loose union of cantons. The **liberals** wanted a stronger federal state and more freedoms. The **Catholic conservatives** wanted to preserve the rights of the cantons and the influence of the Church. In 1841 the canton of **Aargau** closed its monasteries. Many Catholics saw this as a breach of the Federal Pact, and the Aargau monastery dispute poisoned the atmosphere.

In 1844 the canton of **Lucerne** called the **Jesuits** to its higher schools. For liberals and radicals, the Jesuits were a sign of a pro-Rome policy that was hostile to progress. In 1844 and 1845, radical volunteers tried to overthrow the Lucerne government by force. These **volunteer expeditions** failed. They strengthened the Catholic cantons in their resolve to band together.

In 1845 seven cantons founded the **Sonderbund**: Lucerne, Uri, Schwyz, Obwalden and Nidwalden, Zug, Fribourg and Valais. Not all Catholic cantons took part. **Solothurn** was mostly Catholic but was governed by liberals and stood on the side of the Federal Diet. In 1847 the **Federal Diet**, the assembly of the cantons, declared the Sonderbund incompatible with the Federal Pact and decided to dissolve it.

The troops of the Federal Diet were led by the Geneva general **Guillaume-Henri Dufour**. He ordered that the wounded and prisoners be treated with care. The commander of the Sonderbund army was **Johann Ulrich von Salis-Soglio** from the Grisons, a Protestant. This shows that the conflict was not only about religion but also about politics. The war lasted from 3 to 29 November 1847, and in the end Valais surrendered. The losses remained comparatively small.

abschnitte.titel: The road to the federal state
abschnitte.text: After the victory of the Federal Diet, a new **Federal Constitution** was drawn up. It came into force in 1848 and made Switzerland a **federal state**. There was now a common government, the Federal Council, and a parliament with the National Council and the Council of States. The cantons kept many rights of their own, however. The balance between the Confederation and the cantons shapes Switzerland to this day.

gewusst: Dufour later also had the first accurate map of Switzerland produced, the Dufour Map.
The highest peak in Switzerland, the Dufourspitze, is named after General Dufour.

teile.einleitung: The feeding of the five thousand is a well-known miracle story from the Bible. With only five loaves and two fish, thousands of people are fed. The story is in all four Gospels.
wichtigste: There are only five loaves and two fish.
Jesus thanks God, blesses the bread and has it handed out.
About five thousand men are fed, as well as women and children.
Afterwards twelve baskets full of leftovers remain.
In the Gospel of John a boy brings five barley loaves.
The story is in all four Gospels.

abschnitte.text: Many people have followed Jesus to hear him. Evening is coming, and everyone is **hungry**. In the Gospel of John, Jesus asks the disciple **Philip** where bread can be bought. Philip says that even a lot of money would not be enough. The disciples do not know how to feed so many people.

There are only **five loaves** and **two fish**. In the Gospel of John, **Andrew** says that a little **boy** has them with him. They are **barley loaves**, a simple bread of poor people. For so many people it is far too little. Even so, Jesus has the people sit down in groups on the green grass.

Jesus takes the loaves and fish and looks up to heaven. He **gives thanks to God** and blesses the food. Then he breaks the bread and has the disciples hand it out. Everyone eats and is **satisfied**. The Bible mentions about **5,000 men**; according to Matthew, women and children were there as well.

After the meal the disciples gather up the leftover pieces. There are **twelve baskets** full. So there is more left over than there was at the beginning. The number twelve recalls the twelve tribes of Israel and the twelve disciples. In this way the story shows that with God there is enough for everyone.

The feeding of the five thousand is found in **Matthew, Mark, Luke and John**. It is one of the few miracles that all four Gospels tell. Matthew and Mark also report a second feeding, in which four thousand people are fed. Many Christians also see in the story a pointer to the **Lord's Supper**, in which bread is shared.

gewusst: In Tabgha on the Sea of Galilee there is a church with an old mosaic showing a basket of loaves and two fish.
Bread and fish were among the most common foods on the Sea of Galilee.

teile.einleitung: According to Christian belief, every person has a guardian angel who accompanies and protects them. Angels appear in many stories of the Bible and bring messages from God.
wichtigste: According to Christian belief, a guardian angel protects a person.
The word angel means messenger.
In pictures, angels usually have wings.
In the Bible angels often say: “Do not be afraid.”
In pictures the archangel Michael fights a dragon.
The feast of the guardian angels is on 2 October.

abschnitte.text: The word **angel** comes from the Greek “angelos” and means **messenger**. In the Bible, angels bring messages from God to people. Because people are often frightened, angels frequently say first: **“Do not be afraid.”** In pictures, angels usually have **wings**. They show that angels travel between heaven and earth.

According to Christian belief, every person has a **guardian angel**. It accompanies and **protects** them throughout their life. Many children say a guardian angel prayer in the evening **before falling asleep**. When someone has just escaped an accident, people say in everyday life: **They had a guardian angel.** The Catholic Church celebrates the **feast of the guardian angels on 2 October**.

Some angels have a name in the Bible. They are called **archangels**. In many pictures **Michael** fights a **dragon**, as a sign of the victory of good over evil. **Gabriel** brings important messages. According to the Book of Tobit, **Raphael** accompanied the young **Tobias** on his journey and protected him.

Angels can be seen everywhere in churches, in paintings and at Christmas. In the past they were painted as adults with large wings, later often as small children. Even people who are not religious like to give guardian angels as lucky charms, for example as pendants in the car.

gewusst: Raphael's name means “God heals” in Hebrew.
The archangel Michael is the patron saint of many churches, including in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: Simon Peter was one of the twelve apostles and a close friend of Jesus. He was a fisherman on the Sea of Galilee before he followed Jesus. For the Catholic Church he is regarded as the first pope.
wichtigste: Peter was actually called Simon; Jesus gave him the new name.
Peter means “rock”.
His brother Andrew was also a fisherman and a disciple.
After Jesus was arrested, Peter said three times that he did not know him.
In pictures, Peter often carries keys.
St Peter's Basilica in Rome is named after him.

abschnitte.text: Simon was a **fisherman** on the Sea of Galilee, together with his brother **Andrew**. According to the Gospels, Jesus called the two of them with the words that they should now become fishers of men. They left their nets lying and followed him. Simon became one of the twelve apostles. Together with James and John he was one of the disciples closest to Jesus.

Jesus gave Simon a new name: **Cephas** in Aramaic, **Peter** in Greek. Both mean **rock**. Jesus said that he wanted to build his church on this rock. He also promised Peter the **keys of the kingdom of heaven**. That is why Peter is often painted with keys in art.

A well-known story tells how Jesus came to the disciples in the boat, walking on the water. Peter wanted to walk towards him and climbed out of the boat. For a few steps he managed it, but when he saw the strong wind he became **afraid** and began to sink. Jesus stretched out his hand and held him. The story shows Peter as brave, but also as a person with doubts.

Jesus had predicted that Peter would deny him before the **cock** crowed. After Jesus was arrested, Peter was asked whether he belonged to him. **Three times** he said out of fear that he did not know him. Then the cock crowed, and Peter remembered the words of Jesus. He went outside and wept bitterly.

After Easter, Peter became an important leader of the first Christians. According to tradition he later went to **Rome** and died there as a martyr. St Peter's Basilica in Vatican City is said to stand over his grave. According to Catholic teaching, Peter was the first Bishop of Rome and so the **first pope**. Protestant and Orthodox Christians also honour him, but see the office of pope differently.

gewusst: The feast day of Peter and Paul is on 29 June.
St Peter's Basilica is one of the largest churches in the world.

teile.einleitung: The sexton looks after the church building. He or she unlocks the church, prepares the service and tidies up afterwards. In other regions people say “Mesmer” or “Küster”.
wichtigste: In Switzerland the person who looks after the church is called a “Sigrist”, or “Sigristin” for a woman.
The sexton unlocks the church and prepares everything.
In the past he rang the bells by hand.
Before the service he often lights the candles.
For festivals he decorates the church with flowers.
In eastern Switzerland and southern Germany people also say “Mesmer”, in northern Germany “Küster”.

abschnitte.text: The **sexton** (German “Sigrist”) is responsible for the church building. He unlocks the church in the morning and locks it again in the evening. He turns on the lights, provides warmth in winter and keeps everything clean. The word comes from the Latin “sacrista”, someone who looks after holy things. The name **sacristy** comes from the same word, for the room where robes and equipment are kept.

Before the service the sexton prepares everything. He puts out the **hymn books** and puts the numbers of the hymns on the hymn board. He often lights the **candles** on the altar. For baptisms he gets water ready, for the Lord's Supper bread and wine. When people arrive, everything should be ready.

In the past, the **ringing of the bells** was one of the most important tasks. Every day the sexton climbed the tower and pulled the bell ropes. The bells called people to the service, showed the time of day and warned of fire. Today most bells ring electrically. But the sexton often still sets the ringing times.

For festivals such as Christmas, Easter or the harvest thanksgiving, the sexton decorates the church, for example with **flowers**. After the service he puts the hymn books back, puts out the candles and locks up. He also helps at weddings, baptisms and funerals. A woman in this job is called a **Sigristin**. Today many women work as sextons, often in a part-time post with the parish.

gewusst: In Switzerland the sexton is usually employed by the parish, not by the pastor.
In the past the sexton often lived right next to the church in the sexton's house.

teile.einleitung: The Schleitheim Articles are an early confession of faith of the Anabaptists. They were adopted in 1527 in the village of Schleitheim in what is now the canton of Schaffhausen.
wichtigste: The articles were adopted on 24 February 1527.
Schleitheim is in what is now the canton of Schaffhausen.
Michael Sattler is regarded as the main author.
The confession has seven articles.
Christians should not swear oaths at all.
The congregation should keep apart from the world, which it regarded as evil.

abschnitte.text: The **Anabaptists** came into being in the 1520s in Zurich. They were part of the Reformation but wanted to go further than Zwingli. They rejected the baptism of small children and baptised only people who had decided for the faith themselves. The authorities persecuted them harshly. Later the **Mennonites** and the **Amish** grew out of them.

On **24 February 1527**, Anabaptists met in the village of **Schleitheim** in what is now the **canton of Schaffhausen**. There they adopted a shared confession with **seven articles**. **Michael Sattler**, a former monk, is regarded as the main author. He was executed for his faith in the same year.

One article deals with **separation**. It means that the congregation **separates itself from the world**, which it regarded as evil. The Anabaptists wanted to lead a life according to the Bible, apart from violence and worldly customs. Another article concerns the **oath**: Christians should **not swear at all**, because Jesus says so in the Sermon on the Mount.

In the article on the **sword**, the Anabaptists demand that Christians do **not hold any public office that uses the power of the sword**. So they should not become judges or soldiers. Other articles concern baptism, the Lord's Supper, excommunication and the shepherds of the congregation. Non-violence still shapes many Anabaptist congregations today.

gewusst: In Switzerland there are still Anabaptist congregations today, especially in the Emmental and in the Jura.
The Schleitheim Articles were printed quickly and spread widely.
